Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our procurement team has a short marketplace intake for any vendor seeking private and public listing on our vendor portal (we operate across AWS, Azure, GCP). Would Redwood complete our capability worksheet and provide evidence for the technical and commercial sections? Key asks:

- Metering granularity (per-sku, per-instance, per-token where applicable)
- Billing options (Marketplace metered billing vs direct invoicing)
- Tenant isolation and data flow diagrams for private listings

If possible we need a completed worksheet and high-level evidence by end of week (EOW). I attached the Greenline intake as a reference in our internal portal.

Also include any channel/marketplace contacts if there are special onboarding steps for GCP Marketplace.

Best,

Marissa — appreciate the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple clarifications from procurement/tech: 

- Metering: we prefer marketplace-native metered billing for AWS and GCP. For Azure we can accept direct invoicing during pilot but will want to transition to marketplace metering for GA.
- Tenant isolation: we require vendor-managed private listing for any regulated workloads. For non-regulated pilots, per-tenant logical isolation is acceptable.
- Certification: please confirm whether SOC 2 Type II covers the marketplace runtime and whether you can provide a short architecture diagram showing data residency and KMS usage.

Also we will need the order form (DocuSign) to be prepared with the Marketplace SKU IDs once we confirm vendor-side metering. Our timeline aim: initial listing and pilot approval in four weeks.

Can you confirm availability for a joint call Thursday 11:00 PT?

Subject: Re: Request: Cloud marketplace capability worksheet for AWS/Azure/GCP

Alan — hi, Ben from Product Ops here. I pulled together the technical details you asked for and attached an ops notes PDF that maps our marketplace integration paths. High level answers below, with attachments for the detailed fields: marketplace-ops-notes.pdf and kv-cache-ops.pdf (short technical annex).

- Metering: Redwood supports SKU-level metering via the hosted API: we emit per-SKU GUIDs and usage events that can be consumed by AWS Metering Service and the GCP metering endpoint. For tokenized models, our metering translates token-usage into SKU units according to the pricing sheet we shared. See tab "Metering mapping" in the worksheet.
- Billing: We can do both Marketplace-native metered billing and direct invoicing. For marketplace metering we require a one-time seller registration and listing bundle; for direct invoicing we attach a negotiated billing annex in the order form.
- Tenant isolation & private listings: Redwood Private supports vendor-managed private listings within a customer VPC. Data residency is configurable by region; we use customer-managed KMS or HSM for key separation. See architecture diagram in the ops notes. Azure marketplace has an extra listing certification step (we can complete within 7 business days once the legal SKUs are defined).
- Timeline: With completed legal/commercial terms and SKU IDs, AWS/GCP listings can be published within ~2-3 weeks, Azure ~3-4 weeks depending on certification backlog.

Next steps I propose: share a draft DocuSign order form with SKU placeholders and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that lists deliverables and dates. We can provide sample metering event JSON and a sandbox seller account for Greenline to validate.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Product Operations
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: marketplace-ops-notes.pdf (ops diagram, event schema), kv-cache-ops.pdf (for model runtime isolation)
